title: Intro to Application Security
summary: Web apps = client, server, database. Almost every web vuln is untrusted input reaching a dangerous 'sink'. Golden rule: never trust client input.
objectives: Read the theory (client -> server -> sink flow).
Learn the terms 'source' (where input enters) and 'sink' (the dangerous operation).
Learn the golden rule about trusting client input.
Answer the task.
task: The golden rule: should you TRUST data coming from the client? Answer true or false.
hint: The attacker fully controls the request, so the client can never be trusted.

title: Threat Modeling — STRIDE
summary: Threat modeling finds design flaws early. STRIDE = Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.
objectives: Read the six STRIDE categories in the briefing.
Study the flaw: a session token is just base64('username:role').
Decide what the attacker achieves by forging 'admin:admin'.
Match it to ONE STRIDE category and submit that word.
task: Which STRIDE category is a forgeable 'admin:admin' session token? Submit one word.
hint: The attacker pretends to be someone they are not.

title: SAST — find the bug in source
summary: SAST reads source code (without running it) to flag risky patterns, like user input reaching a shell command.
objectives: Open rooms/sast/vulnerable_example.py and read ping_host().
Run: cd rooms/sast && python3 scan.py vulnerable_example.py
Read the line number and the vulnerability class it reports.
Submit that vulnerability class (two words).
task: What vulnerability class does the scanner report on the shell=True line? (two words)
hint: subprocess with shell=True plus user input.

title: DAST — attack the running app
summary: DAST attacks the running app to confirm real exploitability. Classic: reflected XSS, where your input is echoed into the page unescaped.
objectives: Start the appsec app: cd appsec-lab, set up its venv, python3 run_server.py.
In a second terminal, curl /greet with a <script> payload.
See your script reflected unescaped in the response.
Identify the OWASP vuln (3-letter abbreviation) and submit it.
task: Attacking /greet with a <script> payload is which OWASP vuln? (3-letter abbreviation)
hint: Reflected script running in the page.

title: AppSec — capture a real flag
summary: IDOR = returning an object by id with no ownership check. Change the id, read someone else's data.
objectives: Start the CTF target: cd ctf-lab, set up its venv, python3 target/run_target.py.
In a second terminal: curl http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/account/3 (you are NOT admin).
Find the FLAG{...} in the secret_note field.
Submit the exact flag.
task: Exploit the IDOR (GET /api/account/3) and paste the FLAG{...} you captured.
hint: Account id 3 is the admin; the flag is in secret_note.

title: CI/CD Security — the release gate
summary: A DevSecOps gate collects scanner findings and returns an exit code: 0 lets CI continue, non-zero blocks the build.
objectives: cd devsecops-lab.
Run the gate on the samples with --fail-on HIGH (command in the briefing).
Read the FAIL output, then run: echo $? to see the exit code.
Submit that exit code (a number).
task: What exit code does the gate return when it blocks the release? Submit the number.
hint: Non-zero means stop; it is a single digit.
